picks.name: three.quarks
picks.licenseEvidence: LICENSE file: 'Permission is hereby granted, free of charge...' Copyright (c) 2019 Forrest Sun — standard MIT text, verified at raw.githubusercontent.com/Alchemist0823/three.quarks/master/LICENSE
picks.gives: GPU-instanced general-purpose particle/VFX system for three.js (emitters, curves, GPU update) — for embers/sparks in the splash and load-in
picks.where: OASIS splash + load-in ember/spark particle layer
picks.risk: Source file ~100-110KB unminified (observed); gzip size not independently verified — measure after bundling to confirm it fits offline/bundle-size budget. No official GitHub Releases page, only git tags.

picks.name: three.js Lensflare (examples/jsm/objects/Lensflare.js)
picks.licenseEvidence: three.js repo LICENSE file: standard MIT text, 'Copyright © 2010-2026 three.js authors', verified at raw.githubusercontent.com/mrdoob/three.js/dev/LICENSE
picks.gives: Small (~9.8KB source), dependency-free additive-sprite lens-flare/glow technique already part of your three.js dependency — cheapest way to fake volumetric light shafts/glow around light sources
picks.where: Splash screen 'god-ray'-style glow behind the OASIS logo/light source, load-in glow accents
picks.risk: Not true screen-space volumetric god rays (no raymarching) — purely a billboard/sprite trick, so it will look flatter than raymarched god-ray libraries, but avoids the zlib-licensed alternatives entirely.

rejected.name: Kenney Particle Pack
rejected.reason: license not allowed: CC0 1.0 / Public Domain

rejected.name: pmndrs/postprocessing (GodRaysEffect, BloomEffect)
rejected.reason: LICENSE.md is the zlib license (not MIT as commonly assumed) — zlib is not on the allowed license list.

rejected.name: three-good-godrays
rejected.reason: Own LICENSE file is zlib-licensed (Copyright Casey Primozic), and it hard-depends on the zlib-licensed pmndrs/postprocessing package — not allowed.

rejected.name: jeromeetienne/threex.volumetricspotlight
rejected.reason: MIT-licensed but abandoned since 2013 (only 9 commits, pre-dates modern three.js APIs) — too stale/high-risk to integrate, fails the 'active' preference badly.

top: three.quarks (MIT) for GPU embers/sparks, Kenney Particle Pack (CC0) for glow/ember textures, and three.js's own MIT-licensed Lensflare.js for cheap fake volumetric glow — since every real god-ray library in the three.js ecosystem turned out to be zlib-licensed and had to be rejected.
goal: Particles and light for the OASIS splash and load-in: GPU particle systems, light shafts/god rays, glow sprites, embers, volumetric-looking light that is cheap in Three.js
